drafts.title: Headlight beam provides US-appropriate, non-glare illumination
drafts.description: When driving at night on US roads customers experience stable, well-defined low- and high-beam illumination with no excessive glare toward oncoming traffic or sidewalk users and consistent road visibility for the driver.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Vehicle lighting passes the relevant NHTSA/FMVSS photometric test cases for low- and high-beam (as verified in homologation/laboratory photometric tests) and passes a defined on-road glare verification with no more than 5% of controlled test runs flagged for excessive glare by independent observers.
assumptions: NHTSA/FMVSS photometric test procedures and pass/fail thresholds remain the reference for US market verification.
Independent on-road glare verification uses a repeatable protocol with trained observers and standardized routes.
Lighting hardware and software can be adapted within the vehicle architecture for the successor model.
uncertainties: Exact interpretation of customer complaint data vs. regulatory thresholds (some customer reports may reflect local alignment or damage rather than design).
On-road verification outcomes may vary with aftermarket lamps, lens contamination, or misalignment in service vehicles.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation / homologation requirement referenced by the customer signal; compliance and homologation are out of scope for product feature definition here.

drafts.title: Provide physical, non-distracting controls for frequent infotainment and climate functions
drafts.description: Drivers can operate common controls (e.g., volume, temperature, fan speed, seat heating) quickly by touch without looking at the screen, reducing distraction during driving.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At least four frequently used functions have tactile, labeled physical controls reachable from the seated driving position; in a usability test 95% of participants can locate and operate each control within 3 seconds without visual confirmation.
assumptions: Frequent functions for the test set will be defined as: audio volume, driver temperature, fan speed, and seat heating/ventilation.
Usability test participants represent the target driver population (mixed ages, handedness) and use standardized seating/posture.
Vehicle packaging allows integration of dedicated tactile controls near the steering wheel or center console.
uncertainties: Exact number and placement of physical controls that customers consider 'frequent' may vary by region or option pack.
Trade-offs with minimalist interior aesthetics and touch surface integration could constrain placement or size of physical controls.

drafts.title: Provide a clearly measurable increase in rear-seat knee clearance for tall passengers
drafts.description: Rear-seat passengers of height 1.85 m experience noticeably improved knee room so that kneecap contact or extreme discomfort is avoided when the front seats are set to a typical driver position.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: With the front seats set to a standardized driver seating reference, rear-seat knee clearance (measured as horizontal distance from the front seat back surface to the rear passenger knees) is at least 50 mm for a 1.85 m test dummy or human subject; validated in an anthropometric seating test with 95% of tall participants reporting no knee contact.
assumptions: Standardized seating reference points and measurement procedures (e.g., SAE J826-style seating) will be used to measure knee clearance.
50 mm clearance is a practical, perceptible improvement relative to the current model and feasible within successor packaging with moderate architectural changes.
Front-seat travel and typical driver seating positions are preserved to represent realistic use cases.
uncertainties: Achieving the target clearance may require changes to front-seat packaging, seat back thickness, or vehicle floor/seat rails that impact cost, trunk space, or structural design.
Customer perception of 'knee room' is also influenced by seat cushion angle and rear-seat cushion thickness, not only horizontal clearance.

drafts.title: Explicit engineering spec requested for volume control hardware (rotary encoder)
drafts.description: Customers requesting a tactile volume control expressed a specific hardware preference for a rotary encoder with precise electrical and resolution characteristics.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A rotary encoder meeting 12-bit resolution and a 48 V supply specification is defined and documented for engineering evaluation / procurement.
assumptions: The customer's request is an engineering-level specification rather than a purely customer-facing outcome.
Implementing a 12-bit encoder and 48 V supply may require changes to infotainment electrical architecture and supplier sourcing.
uncertainties: The requested 48 V supply and 12-bit resolution may conflict with vehicle electrical architecture choices or EMC and safety requirements.
Customers asked for a specific component spec; alternative solutions (e.g., high-resolution encoder at different supply voltage) might deliver equivalent user experience.
drafts.scope_reason: This is an engineering / component specification rather than a customer-facing requirement and is therefore out of scope for product-level requirements.

drafts.title: Customer request for lower base price and better business case
drafts.description: Multiple customers report the base vehicle price is too high and explicitly requested a price reduction of about $5,000 to improve perceived value.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Achieve a base MSRP at launch that is at least $5,000 lower than the reported current-model baseline for an equivalent configuration (or provide an alternative entry variant meeting that pricing target).
assumptions: The $5,000 target is measured against a clearly defined baseline configuration of the current model in the same market and currency.
Pricing and packaging changes are a cross-functional business decision influenced by cost, options, and market positioning.
uncertainties: Market conditions, supplier costs, and features included in the base configuration may prevent achieving the requested absolute price reduction without trade-offs.
Customers may accept alternative value propositions (e.g., more features at the same price) rather than a direct price cut.
drafts.scope_reason: Pricing and business-case targets are out of scope for engineering product requirements.
